questions.question: 下面两档节目：一档是纯搞笑的综艺，观众都知道只是消遣；另一档把总统候选人辩论包装成真人秀，按「上镜感」打分。波兹曼会怎样评价？
options: 两者同样有害，因为电视娱乐本身就会麻痹观众
综艺更有害，因为它占走了观众本可读书的时间
辩论秀更好，因为它至少让更多人关注了政治
综艺无伤大雅，把辩论做成秀才是真正的危险
questions.explanation: 波兹曼从不反对娱乐本身，他明说纯娱乐节目无伤大雅，电视做这类事做得相当好。他的靶子是电视把本不该娱乐化的新闻、政治、宗教、教育也做成了娱乐——问题不在于电视提供娱乐，而在于一切都以娱乐的方式呈现。把本书读成反对看电视，是最大的误读。
questions.question_en: Two programs: one is pure comedy that viewers know is just for fun; the other packages a presidential debate as a reality show scored on how candidates look on camera. How would Postman judge them?
options_en: Both are equally harmful, because TV entertainment itself numbs its viewers
The comedy is worse, because it eats time viewers could have spent reading
The debate show is better, because it at least gets more people into politics
The comedy is harmless; turning the debate into a show is the real danger
questions.explanation_en: Postman never opposes entertainment as such; he says plainly that junk TV is harmless and that television does it well. His target is television turning news, politics, religion and education into entertainment — the problem is not that TV entertains but that everything is presented as entertainment. Reading the book as anti-TV is its most common misreading.

questions.question: 按波兹曼的分析，电报（早于电视）给公共话语带来的最根本的改变是什么？
options: 让新闻必须配上主播和片头音乐，才能抢到受众越来越短的注意力
让图像第一次取代文字，成为公共话语中占主导地位的表达方式
大量你无法据以行动的远方信息涌入，「知道」从此和「有用」分了家
让政府能更有效地审查和隐瞒消息，公众因此失去了获取真相的可靠渠道
questions.explanation: 波兹曼说电报第一次让信息与行动脱钩，并用「信息-行动比」来量：千里之外与你无关的事件源源不断涌来，你动容却什么也做不了，信息退化成消费品，还带来去语境化的碎片。审查与隐瞒是奥威尔式的担忧；图像取代文字、主播和配乐则是后来照片与电视的事。
questions.question_en: According to Postman, what was the most fundamental change the telegraph (before television) brought to public discourse?
options_en: It forced news to come with anchors and theme music to win audiences' shrinking attention
It let images replace print for the first time as the dominant form of public expression
A flood of distant information you could not act on, so that knowing came apart from being useful
It let governments censor and conceal news more effectively, cutting the public off from the truth
questions.explanation_en: Postman says the telegraph first severed information from action, measured by the information-action ratio: a stream of distant, irrelevant events moves you but leaves nothing to do, so information becomes a commodity, and it arrives as decontextualized fragments. Censorship is Orwell's fear; images overtaking print, anchors and music came later with photography and television.

questions.question: 波兹曼把麦克卢汉的「媒介即讯息」推进成「媒介即隐喻」「媒介即认识论」。推进的那一步说的是什么？
options: 媒介的内容常被扭曲，所以要先核实信息再判断真假
媒介本身比它承载的内容更重要，真正改变社会的是媒介
不同媒介适合不同内容，严肃话题应该回到书面讨论
主导媒介悄悄决定了一个文化凭什么认定一件事为真
questions.explanation: 「媒介本身比内容更重要」是麦克卢汉原句的意思，波兹曼在此之上再进一步：一个文化认定什么算真理的标准，是被它主导的媒介决定的——同一句谚语在口传部落里是判案依据，在法庭上是笑话。他要你先问这个媒介天生偏爱哪一种真理，而不只是问信息真不真。
questions.question_en: Postman pushed McLuhan's "the medium is the message" further, into "the medium is the metaphor" and media as epistemology. What does that extra step claim?
options_en: Media content is often distorted, so information must be verified before judging it true
The medium matters more than the content it carries; media are what really change society
Different media suit different content, so serious topics should return to written debate
The dominant medium quietly decides on what grounds a culture counts something as true
questions.explanation_en: "The medium matters more than its content" is what McLuhan's line already meant; Postman goes further: a culture's very criteria for truth are set by its dominant medium — a proverb that settles a dispute in an oral tribe is a joke in a courtroom. He wants you to ask which kind of truth a medium favors, not just whether a given message is true.
